_comment: The model catalog the Models screen offers. Adding a model is editing this file — no code.
Entries must name a repo that holds an EXPORTED MobileTransformers package (one carrying a
mobiletransformers_manifest.json at its root), not a plain Hugging Face model. `fromPretrained`
reads the manifest first to plan the download, so a base HF repo id fails at the first request.
then push it to the Hub — or run `make publish-catalog`, which exports, gate-checks and pushes
this whole shelf and is the producer these entries are kept in sync with.
Set published=false for a package that is not on the Hub yet: the entry stays visible with a
badge and a disabled Install, which is more useful than an entry that 404s on tap.
approxSizeMb is the INFERENCE GROUP alone, and every figure below is measured off the pushed
package's manifest (sum of fileSizes under inference/ plus the tokenizer), not estimated.
Requesting train or rag adds to it — the rag group is ~91 MB for every decoder here, because it
is the same all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedder in each.

models.description: The smallest useful chat model here, and the one every parity check is measured against. Fastest to pull and fastest to train, so it is the right first model on a new device.
models.recommendedFor: First run, Chat, and the fastest training loop

models.description: Gemma-3 270M tuned for function calling: it turns an instruction into a structured call that the app's allowlist then validates before anything runs. Small enough to fine-tune on a phone in minutes.
models.recommendedFor: Tool calls, and the on-device fine-tuning demo

models.description: The MARS entry. Multi-Adapter Rank Sharing is this project's own fine-tuning method: instead of one adapter per layer, layers share a down-projection, so the trainable parameter count grows with rank rather than with depth — 279,936 parameters here against a 268M backbone. Pick this one to see what the research is actually about.
models.recommendedFor: MARS, and comparing a shared-adapter fine-tune against LoRA

models.description: A noticeably more fluent decoder at roughly four times SmolLM2's size. Generation on a mid-range phone is a few tokens per second — worth seeing, because it is the honest cost of the extra quality.
models.recommendedFor: Chat quality, and the memory ceiling on smaller devices

models.description: The sentence encoder behind retrieval, and the only entry that is useful on its own without a decoder: install it alone and the app shows Models, Retrieval, Train and Federated, hiding Chat because an embedding model has no generative head. Exported as text-classification rather than feature-extraction — that is what makes an encoder trainable at all — so it also carries a classification head. That head is randomly initialised with LABEL_0/LABEL_1 labels, which is why Classify stays hidden: the head is the part fine-tuning is meant to learn, not something the checkpoint ships.
models.recommendedFor: Retrieval on its own, and the smallest possible training run

models.description: A sentiment classifier with real trained labels (NEGATIVE / POSITIVE), so the Classify screen has something to say from the first tap — unlike the MiniLM encoder, whose head is randomly initialised. An encoder, so Chat and Retrieval are hidden for it; fine-tuning it on your own labels is the point.
models.recommendedFor: Classify, and fine-tuning a classifier on device
